description: Server-side PKI work on the local TLS gateway: the admin-console client certificate (CN=audit) was compromised; mint a new CA-signed client certificate for CN=auditor, revoke the compromised one by publishing crl/crl.pem, and write report/pki.md with new_cert_serial, revoked_serial and crl_path. The offline gate checks.py re-derives everything from the files with openssl. Needs openssl on PATH and in the run's --auto-approve (not in the default set).

criteria: The agent minted a fresh client certificate for CN=auditor signed by the existing DemoCorp CA (clientAuth EKU, key kept alongside), published crl/crl.pem listing exactly the compromised audit serial, and left the CA, the gate, the incident note and the README untouched.

python3 checks.py passes: the new certificate verifies against pki/ca.crt, the CRL verifies against the CA and lists exactly the compromised serial, and report/pki.md's new_cert_serial, revoked_serial and crl_path match the re-derived values.
